A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SUPE research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved between sections.

before.justification: V1 reports original reinforcement-learning experiments on AntMaze, Visual AntMaze and Kitchen, including exploration measurements and appendix ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and adds OGBench evaluations, hyperparameter studies and offline-data-quality experiments.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, trajectory-VAE training, optimistic relabeling, frozen low-level skills and high-level online learning remain unchanged. The larger networks and different hyperparameter values are configurations for added experiments.

E1.justification: The main evaluation expands from 19 tasks across three domains to 42 across seven, adding HumanoidMaze, AntSoccer, Cube and Scene. These introduce harder humanoid control, ball manipulation and additional sequential manipulation tasks. Appendices H.3 and J.1 also add AntMaze play and expert-to-random data scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in matched experiments is retained, including the KL, ICVF and ExPLORe-without-online-RND comparisons. HILP with Offline Data already appears in v1; the new SPiRL discussion clarifies an existing baseline. Added datasets use existing comparison methods.

E3.justification: Main figures switch from mean summaries to interquartile means. Added OGBench experiments introduce larger networks, a 0.995 discount and domain-specific KL and baseline-tuning settings; new studies vary skill horizons and RND coefficients. Retained-domain settings largely persist. V2's blanket -1/0 reward statement conflicts with its detailed Kitchen description, so a Kitchen reward-protocol change is not established.

E4.justification: Section 5.5 and Appendix G add seven-task sensitivity studies for RND coefficients and skill horizons. Appendix J.1 tests dependence on expert, navigate, stitch and noisy exploratory data. The original ICVF, KL, coverage and data-corruption analyses remain, with several relocated.

E5.justification: V2 introduces explicit IQM summaries with 95% stratified bootstrap confidence intervals and specifies t-tests at p=0.05 for Table 3's significance markings. Appendix shading is explicitly defined as standard error. Kitchen's 16 seeds were already documented in v1, so this is not an established increase. V2 contains conflicting four-versus-eight-seed statements for manipulation and AntSoccer experiments.

E6.justification: New results include SUPE's success on large and giant HumanoidMaze tasks where evaluated baselines fail, HILP with Offline Data's advantage on Scene, and SUPE's failure on noisy Explore data. Sensitivity and play-dataset results are also added. Every numerical entry in v1 Table 1 is retained in v2 Table 3; changed IQM aggregates are different summaries, not demonstrated same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The MDP formulation, VAE loss, trajectory-relabeling equations and RND/reward-model objectives are retained. No substantive mathematical assumptions, definitions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contribution: using unlabeled trajectories for both skill pretraining and online high-level learning to improve sparse-reward exploration. Expanded experiments do not redefine that contribution or its stated core claim.

C2.justification: Appendix J.1 adds consequential applicability qualifications: noisy data can yield unusable skills, while expert data reduces the need for structured exploration and thus SUPE's advantage. Section 5.3 interprets HILP's Scene performance as support for the broader data-reuse principle. These substantially extend the interpretation despite retaining Section 6's original limitations.

D1.justification: Appendices A-C substantially expand hardware and compute reporting, domain-specific architecture and hyperparameter tables, and Diffusion BC + JSRL tuning details. Appendix J.1 documents expert-data collection and its VAE KL-coefficient sweep. Existing code-access statements remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds substantial hierarchical-RL positioning, contrasting jointly learned primitives with frozen pretrained skills and citing additional classical HRL and motor-primitive work. OGBench and statistical-evaluation references are added, while Liu and Abbeel (2021) is removed.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative and appendices are substantially reorganized. Detailed domain descriptions move to Appendix D, coverage analysis leaves the main text, and Section 5.5 becomes a hyperparameter study. Appendices regroup D4RL, OGBench and data-quality results, while introductory and method prose largely persist.

P2.justification: The domain montage and aggregate-results grid expand substantially, and first-goal times gain an IQM interval plot. New sensitivity and data-quality displays accompany relocated figures and tables: v1 Table 1 and Figures 4-5 become v2 Table 3 and Figures 10 and 13. Plot styling and hyperparameter-table layouts also change.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the empirical basis by testing qualitatively harder domains and directly examining previously untested hyperparameter and data-quality dependencies. Reporting failures and explaining applicability boundaries makes the evidence more informative, while explicit confidence intervals and significance procedures improve assessability. Conflicting seed counts and the Kitchen reward-summary inconsistency weaken reproducibility, but these localized defects do not outweigh the substantial gains.
